newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Menem sees mortgage bank sale bill by next week.
newsitem.headline: Menem sees mortgage bank sale bill by next week.

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem said Tuesday that Congress will pass a bill to privatize the state mortgage lender Banco Hipotecario this week or next.
"This week or next we will have the privatization law to be able to do public works and create new jobs," Menem told foreign correspondents, when asked how proceeds from the sale would be used.
Menem said the law passed will be the same as the one originally proposed by the government and will not include modifications sought by Congress.
Plans to sell Hipotecario were launched last September and sparked criticism in the ruling Peronist Party and among the opposition. It has the largest assets of any Argentine bank, at $4.31 billion.
Banco Hipotecario made a profit last year of $306 million, versus $327 million a year earlier.

Menem also said that he was prepared to wait several months longer to see if politicians, business leaders and trade unions can reach agreement on labor reforms rather than having to implement them by decree.
"I aim to finish with the laws and have them in place before the elections," Menem said in reference to October mid-term legislative elections.
"I don't care about the political cost. This is not a government driven by elections," the president said.

Menem said the government hoped to reduce unemployment by three to five percentage points this year with the help of the reforms that have sparked widespread opposition. The jobless rate is currently just over 17 percent.

The president also gave details of an agreement with Brazil in compensation for Brazilian subsidies for investment in the north east of its territory. Argentina has been allowed a quota of about 100,000 cars in the next few years, he said.
